title: Practice 3: Two verbs for every way of going

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Ты ___ (ехать — to go by vehicle, ride, one way) в Рио на Олимпиаду?
exercises.why: **едешь** is the present tense (2nd person singular) of **ехать** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ездить** for many directions. present: я е́ду · ты е́дешь · он е́дет · мы е́дем · вы е́дете · они е́дут. — Wiktionary, «ехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb ехать refers to going by some means of transportation, i.e. riding, driving: Я еду на поезде. (Я иду пешком.) Я еду в Европу. (Я иду в комнату.) This verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан едет в город.» · «Он редко ездит в город.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Сегодня вечером мы едем в город.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Are you coming to Rio for the Olympics?
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Над водой ___ (летать — to fly, there and back or in general) чайки.
exercises.why: **летают** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **летать** (to fly) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **лететь** for one direction. present: я лета́ю · ты лета́ешь · он лета́ет · мы лета́ем · вы лета́ете · они лета́ют. — Wiktionary, «летать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Летать: this verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Like the verb "ходить" (по комнате) the verb "летать" may be used to indicate motion without a definite goal. Note. — Do not confuse the following: Самолёт летает над городом. (motion without a definite goal) — Самолёт летит над городом. (motion towards a definite goal) — both: The aircraft is flying over the city.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Капитан летит в Вашингтон.» · «Он иногда летает в Вашингтон.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Она ___ (ходить — to go, walk, there and back or in general) на каблуках.
exercises.why: **ходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **ходить** (to go, to walk) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **идти** for one direction. present: я хожу́ · ты хо́дишь · он хо́дит · мы хо́дим · вы хо́дите · они хо́дят. — Wiktionary, «ходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  Compare: «Ребёнок ходит шесть месяцев.» (The child has been walking for six months.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

This verb belongs to the 1st conjugation (characterized by the vowel -ё-, like живу, -ёшь, -ёт …).» — DLI, Lessons 19–20. exercises.why: **едут** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **ехать** (to go (by horse or vehicle), to ride, to drive) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ездить** for many directions. present: я е́ду · ты е́дешь · он е́дет · мы е́дем · вы е́дете · они е́дут. — Wiktionary, «ехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The basic meaning of the verbs идти, ехать, лететь is being actually on the way to some place: Мы идём в кино. Мы едем в город. Мы летим в Нью-Йорк. — right now.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  «The verb ехать refers to going by some means of transportation, i.e. riding, driving: Я еду на поезде. (Я иду пешком.) Я еду в Европу. (Я иду в комнату.) This verb belongs to the 1st (Е) type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lessons 19–20.  Compare: «Капитан едет в город.» · «Он редко ездит в город.» — DLI, Lesson 22. «Сегодня вечером мы едем в город.» — DLI, Lesson 20.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Our neighbours are travelling to the Baltic Sea in July.
exercises.context: Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Пешки ___ (ходить — to go, walk, there and back or in general) только вперёд.
exercises.why: **ходят** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **ходить** (to go, to walk) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **идти** for one direction. present: я хожу́ · ты хо́дишь · он хо́дит · мы хо́дим · вы хо́дите · они хо́дят. — Wiktionary, «ходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The present tense of all Russian verbs has a twofold function; it indicates: A. an action in progress ("actual" function); B. a repeated or habitual action ("repeated" function). However each action of going (to go on foot, to ride, to fly) is expressed in Russian by two parallel verbs: one for the function A — being on the way to … — иду, еду, лечу; another for the function B — usually, often, etc. to go to … (the motion to and from is understood) — хожу, езжу, летаю.» — DLI, Lesson 22.  «Ходить, ездить: these two verbs belong to the 2nd (И) type of conjugation. Notice that the consonant д changes into ж in the first person singular (like видеть — вижу — видишь).» — DLI, Lesson 22.  Compare: «Ребёнок ходит шесть месяцев.» (The child has been walking for six months.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
